# Mega Remediation: file issues + fix all the things (Sonnet-granular work packets)

## Context

A full diagnostic session (2026-07-01) root-caused "diarization doesn't work" to a **capture bug**: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` reads the input format once at setup (`CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144`) and has no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer, so a mid-session device sample-rate change makes the converter use a stale ratio — production WAVs are time-stretched 1.6–1.9×, corrupting transcription timestamps and diarization alignment. Two more production bugs surfaced: `-mic-cleaned.wav` files are pure digital silence (−180 dB), and `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment` never writes/clears `word_timings` (stale timings survive re-diarization).

The same session fixed all test suites (Record-ML now 314/314 green, uncommitted) and triaged ~55 open issues. Verification against main shows **several open issues are already fixed** (#190, #191, #193, #194, #205, most of F22) — they need regression-test-and-close, not fixes. The user folded **Epic 30** (#202, audit findings F1–F27 from `docs/codebase-audit-20260612-142636.md`) and the **contract-audit criticals** (#211–#213) into this plan. The prior Epic 30 plan (`~/.claude/plans/atomic-roaming-graham.md`) is the spec source for F-numbers but predates the GRDB migration — file paths below are corrected to current main.

**Goal**: every packet is small enough for a Sonnet agent to execute alone: one fix, explicit files, verify-first, TDD, one commit.

## Ground rules (embed in every agent prompt)

- **Scope**: touch ONLY the files listed in your packet. If the fix genuinely requires another file, stop and report back instead of editing it.
- **Verify first**: confirm the defect still exists on main before writing code. If already fixed, write the missing regression test (if any), then report `ALREADY_FIXED` with file:line evidence — do not "improve" working code.
- **TDD**: failing test first (RED), confirm failure via the package's `swift test --filter`, then implement (GREEN). Swift Testing (`@Test`/`#expect`), not XCTest.
- **Layering**: Domain → Foundation only; Business → Domain; Presentation never imports Infrastructure. File caps: Domain 100 / Business 300 / Infrastructure 300 / ViewModels 200 / Views 150 lines.
- **Impact check**: before editing a symbol, find its callers (`gitnexus_impact` if available, else grep) and list them in your report.
- **Commits**: one commit per fix, format `fix(scope): description (#issue)`. No Claude/Anthropic attribution. Never touch theme files (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/Theme/`, `Resources/`, `*Theme*Tests`).
- **gh**: always `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh …`.
- **Tests per package**: `cd <pkg> && swift test` for Record-Foundation/Record-Audio/Record-ML; root `swift test` for the rest. Only ONE agent runs tests in a given package at a time (lane rule).
- **Model**: Sonnet for all packets unless marked `[main-loop]` (done by the orchestrator directly).

## Phase 0 — Bookkeeping `[main-loop]`

**0.1 Commit the session's uncommitted fixes** (before any agent edits, so packets diff cleanly):
- `fix(record-ml tests): monorepo paths, vacuous OSLog test, MCPLifecycle root + FD allowance` — 12 test files under `Record-ML/Tests/Unit/`
- `fix(record-ml): raise semantic cache threshold 0.10→0.55` — `CachingContextProvider.swift`, `SemanticCacheTests.swift`
- `fix(record-ml): isArmed accessor + poll-for-arm flake fix (#198)` — `CalendarAwareMeetingDetector.swift`, `CalendarAwareMeetingDetectorTests.swift`
- `refactor(record-ml): GRDBContextCache complexity` — `GRDBContextCache.swift`
- `test(record-ml): disable keychain access-group test pending entitlements (#125)` — `CredentialStoreTests.swift`
- Record-Foundation mocks/ISO8601, Record-Audio stale-path tests + AudioSessionDetector permission gate, Record-App `MockStorageEngine.swift` — one commit per package.
- **Leave uncommitted**: all Record-Presentation modified files (theme WIP intermixed) except after hunk-level review shows a purely-localization hunk; when ambiguous, skip.
- Then create branch `fix/mega-remediation-20260701` from main for all remaining work (local-only; no push/PR unless asked).

**0.2 File the three new issues** from `.temp/issue-drafts-20260701.md`: write the three body files it references, run its three `gh issue create` commands. Record the new issue numbers — packets A1, A6, M1 reference them.

**0.3 Post this plan as a comment on #202** (standing plans-to-GH-issues preference), noting Epic 30 is folded in.

## Wave 1 — Verify-and-close packets (parallel, read-mostly, cheap)

Each: confirm fix exists on main at the cited site, add a regression test **only if none exists**, comment evidence on the issue, close it (authorized).

| Packet | Issue | Evidence site on main | Regression test if missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | #190 AEC truncation | `AECProcessorActor.swift:125–170` remainder+chunk loop | `output.count == input.count` for 1,365-sample input |
| V2 | #191 ID mismatch | `StartRecordingUseCase.swift:119,127` single sessionID threaded | AudioFile.id == session.id assertion |
| V3 | #193 WAV deleted on DB fail | `StopAndTranscribeUseCase.swift:72–90` — deletes only on cancellation, preserves on storage throw | mock storage throws → file still exists |
| V4 | #194 silent converter errors | `ConverterErrorTracker` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:230) + `MicTapBridge.handleConverterError:109` | threshold-terminates stream |
| V5 | #205 symlink escape | `ObsidianProvider.swift:32–34` trailing-slash guard | symlinked file outside vault skipped |
| V6 | #189 + #138 stale test paths / FD flake | fixed in Phase 0 commits | none needed — cite commits |

## Wave 2 — Audio money path (Record-Audio lane, SERIAL — same files)

**A1 — System tap ignores mid-session sample-rate change (new issue from 0.2; THE diarization root cause).**
Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift`, `CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift`, new `CoreAudioTapCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`, tests.
Mirror the #49 pattern from `MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift:16–77` (`handleConfigurationChange()`): observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` on the tap engine; on fire, remove tap, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild `AVAudioConverter` + tap closure (reuse continuation + writer + `tapT0`), restart engine. Defensive second layer: inside the tap callback compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` to the converter's assumed input rate; on mismatch log and trigger the rebuild (buffer's own format is authoritative). Remove observer in `cleanup()`. RED test: source-inspection test that the observer registration exists (behavioral CoreAudio tests can't run headless) + unit test of the ratio math via a rebuildable converter seam if feasible.

**A2 — #192 remainder: main tap WAVWriter has no errorHandler (F3).**
Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift:97–101`, test.
`WAVCleanedAudioSink` already wires it (F22 done, `errorHandler` is `public let`). Wire the tap's writer identically: handler finishes the session stream with `.writeFailed` and logs. Verify `_totalSamplesWritten` increments only on success (`WAVWriter.swift` ~99–130) — fix if not.

**A3 — F11: `stop()` duration from `wavWriter.totalSamplesWritten`, not wall clock.** Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift` (~:265). Remove `try? … ?? 0` / `?? Date()` silent fallbacks (DPS-204). Note: after A1 lands, samples-written is the honest duration even across rate changes.

**A4 — F27: create WAVWriter inside the `do` block** so failed starts don't orphan 44-byte WAVs. Files: `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor.swift:95–101` (note the existing `defer state` guard at :89–92 — keep it correct).

**A5 — #223: `abortRouteChange(with:)` dead code — wire it, don't delete it.**
Files: `MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`. It performs the *complete* cleanup (observer removal, voice-processing off, engine teardown) that `handleConfigurationChange()`'s three failure paths skip (they only set state + finish continuation, leaking observer/engine). Replace those failure paths with `abortRouteChange(with:)` calls. RED: source-inspection test that failure paths call it.

**A6 — Silent mic-cleaned WAV investigation (new issue from 0.2).**
Files: `AECProcessorActor.swift`, `WAVCleanedAudioSink.swift`, the far-end feed site (`RecordingStateViewModelStreaming.swift` — read-only for diagnosis), integration test file.
The writer chain is healthy (correct duration, errorHandler wired) — the silence enters upstream. Steps: (1) integration test: synthetic 440 Hz sine through `AECProcessorActor.process()` with silent far-end → assert non-zero output RMS; (2) same with far-end == mic signal (self-cancellation hypothesis) — if output goes to zero, the bug is the far-end wiring feeding mic as its own echo reference; (3) add a cheap guard in `AECProcessorActor`: log-once when N consecutive processed frames are all-zero while input RMS > threshold. Report findings; if the root cause is outside listed files, report back rather than fix.

**A7 — #198 remainder: fixed sleeps → polling** in `AudioSessionDetectorTests.swift:26`, `AudioSessionDetectorCoreAudioTests.swift:21` (Record-Audio) and `CalendarAwareMeetingDetectorTests.swift:130,166,201` (Record-ML — coordinate with ML lane). Build the F9 `waitForEvent(in:timeout:)` deadline helper (ContinuousClock) once per package; the `isArmed` polling pattern from Phase 0 is the model.

## Wave 3 — Record-ML lane (serial within lane; parallel to Wave 2)

**M1 — word_timings upsert gap (new issue from 0.2).** Files: `Record-ML/Sources/MLInfrastructure/Storage/GRDBSQL.swift:101–108`, `GRDBStorageActor+Diarization.swift:39–44`, tests. Add `word_timings` to `upsertSegment` (insert + `excluded` update), encode `seg.wordTimings` via `JSONEncoder` (nil → NULL) at the `attachDiarization` call site. RED: attach twice with different timings → second read returns second timings; attach with nil → NULL (not stale).

**M2 — #195/F6: FluidDiarizationPlugin re-entrancy.** Files: `FluidDiarizationPlugin.swift:167–188`, timeout test file. In-flight guard serializing `diarize()` (actor-state flag + `while` wait, or queue continuations); fix the misleading isolation comment at :163–165; cancel the detached task when `withTimeout` fires (currently orphaned). RED: two concurrent `diarize()` calls → second waits (no concurrent inference), timeout cancels underlying task.

**M3 — #197/F8: unmanaged `Task { await self.start() }` in init.** Files: `CalendarAwareMeetingDetector.swift` (init at ~:32). Store the handle, cancel in a `shutdown()`/`deinit`. Careful: Phase 0 added `isArmed` here — rebase on committed state.

**M4a — F13**: log the JSON parse error in `MCPSummarizationPlugin.swift` (~:179), not just the payload.
**M4b — F14**: missing prompt template throws at load instead of `?? ""` in `SummarizationPrompts.swift` (~:51).
**M4c — F15**: stop mapping every EventKit failure to `.accessDenied` in `Calendar/EventStore.swift` (~:20).
Three separate packets, one commit each.

**M5 — F12: failed ROLLBACK logging** — verify GRDB equivalent. GRDB's `dbPool.write` manages transactions itself; if no manual rollback exists anymore, report `OBSOLETE_POST_GRDB` and close the finding in the tracking comment.

**M6 — F23: atomic temp-file-rename writes** in `JSONSpeakerProfileStore.swift` (~:88–127).

**M7 — F16: honest `isPluggedIn`** via real power-source query (IOKit `IOPSCopyPowerSourcesInfo`) or `nil`, not `battery == 100`. `InferenceTelemetry.swift` (~:57).

**M8a — F24**: timeout errors read `TimeoutConfig` instead of hardcoded 300 — `WhisperKitPlugin.swift` (~:217), `WhisperKitProPlugin.swift` (~:195). **M8b — F25**: transcript-length log → `privacy: .private` in `AppleFoundationModelsPlugin.swift` (~:59).

## Wave 4 — App/Presentation/Pro lane (parallel to Waves 2–3)

**P1 — #196/F7: SearchViewModel generic catch** (`Record-Presentation/Sources/Presentation/ViewModels/SearchViewModel.swift` ~:53): set a generic `searchError` + log, clear stale prior error. RED: non-UserFacingError throw → error surfaced, not empty results.

**P2 — F17**: extract the shared ~140-line streaming loop from the two `transcribeStream` overloads in `StreamingTranscriptionUseCase.swift` (keep dropped-yield logging in both).

**P3 — F20 + #224 (Record-Pro)**: fix `PipelineRunner.swift:261–266` empty `rawResponse` debug dump (capture the real failed response or delete the path); delete dead `mergeSpeakers` at `PipelineRunner.swift:276` (verify zero callers first — issue said 3 copies, only 1 remains).

**P4 — F26 + warnings sweep**: delete `#expect(Bool(true))` tautologies (`MeetingAppMonitorTests.swift:59`, `AudioFileLoaderTests.swift:86`); fix `internal(set)` warning `MicCaptureActor.swift:38`; unused `meetingDetector` `AppAssemblerBuilders.swift:227`.

**P5 — F18: MenuBarViewModel split** (502 lines across 5 extension files → real units under the 200-line ViewModel cap). **P6 — F19: InferenceMetrics.swift split** (Domain 100-line cap). Both are refactors — run LAST in this lane, after P1–P4 commit, since they move code others reference.

## Wave 5 — MCP provider wiring (Unit E — sequenced, one packet per step)

Spec from the Epic 30 plan §Unit E with GRDB renames (`DuckDBContextCache` → `GRDBContextCache`, already exists and was refactored in Phase 0):
1. **E1** `NotionProvider.isHealthy()` three-way fix (nil credential → false; `keychainReadFailed` logged distinctly → false; optional 3s `GET /v1/users/me` ping). Keep `Bool`.
2. **E2** Cache provider-scoping: add `provider_id` to exact + semantic get/put in `GRDBContextCache` + `GRDBSQL` cache statements; `CachingContextProvider` passes `inner.providerID`. RED: cross-provider isolation test. (Build on the 0.55-threshold work from Phase 0.)
3. **E3** `AppConfig` fields `obsidianVaultPath: String?`, `notionEnabled = false` (`decodeIfPresent`; update memberwise-copy sites in `Record-App/Sources/TheRecord/App.swift`). **Pre-check**: if the app is sandboxed (check entitlements), vault path must be a security-scoped bookmark `Data` — report before implementing.
4. **E4** Wire in `AppAssembler.buildMCPProviders` (`AppAssemblerBuilders.swift` ~:141): `KeychainCredentialStore` + `migrateAccessibilityIfNeeded()`, `GRDBContextCache` at `Directories.appSupport` when `config.contextCache.enabled`, wrap every provider in `CachingContextProvider`; degrade to uncached on cache-init throw.
5. **E5** Settings "Integrations" tab: consumer-side `IntegrationSettingsStore` protocol in Presentation (layer rule), adapter at composition root; Notion toggle + SecureField, Obsidian folder picker, "Test connection" button. Restart-required v1.
6. **E6** Integration test: ObsidianProvider against temp vault through full `QueryContextUseCase` chain; cache hit on second query (`RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1`).

## Wave 6 — Contract-audit criticals (#211–#213) — after Wave 5 (E4 touches the same assembler)

Each packet starts by reading its issue body (`unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue view <n>`), which is the spec:
- **C1 — #211 DiskSpaceMonitor**: dead feature, zero production implementation → implement + wire (aligns with GA #124 storage guard; minimal v1: warn below threshold before recording start).
- **C2 — #212 ModelDownloadDelegate**: unwired delegate → connect download progress to the consuming view model.
- **C3 — #213 PrivacyModeProvider**: 11 consumers get nil → wire a real provider at the composition root (default `PrivacyMode.default`).

## Wave 7 — Verification & review `[main-loop orchestrated]`

1. **Full suites, ratchet-only**: `Record-Foundation`, `Record-Audio`, `Record-ML` (baseline 314/49 green), root package. Known allowed failure: root `MiscLintTests` ThemeEditorView 786>500 (theme WIP, explicitly deprioritized — do not fix).
2. **3-round adversarial review** (user's standing pattern): Round 1 per-lane reviewers (audio / ML / app+presentation / MCP), Round 2 cross-dimensional (concurrency, layering, silent-failure), Round 3 one mega-adversary trying to disprove the two headline fixes (A1 rate-change, A6 silence) with a synthesizer verdict. Sonnet agents; findings → fix packets or logged.
3. **Re-run the epic-28 AEC verification harness** after A6 (epic-28 numbers were measured with #190 in place) — update CHANGELOG/CURRENT_STATE numbers if present.
4. `swiftlint` clean on touched files; `gitnexus_detect_changes()` before final commits if index is fresh.
5. Close issues fixed by this work with evidence comments: #192, #195, #196, #197, #198, #211, #212, #213, #223, #224, the three new issues, plus Wave 1's closures. Comment progress on #202.

## Orchestration mechanics

- **Canary first** (pre-flight rule): run V5 (#205 verify-and-close, smallest packet) alone; on success launch the rest of Wave 1 in parallel, then start lanes.
- Lanes = packages; packets within a lane run serially (build-dir + file contention), lanes run in parallel (max 4 concurrent agents).
- Agents get: the ground-rules block, their packet spec verbatim, exact file paths, and the package test command. `model: sonnet` on every Agent call.
- Orchestrator (main loop) reviews each agent's report + diff before the next packet in that lane starts; failed packets get one retry with the error trace, then escalate to Opus/main-loop.
- Everything stays local on `fix/mega-remediation-20260701` — no push/PR unless the user asks.

## Estimate

~35 packets: 6 verify-and-close, ~20 small fixes, A1/A6/E-series/C-series meaty. Largest risks: A1 (CoreAudio, hard to test headless — lean on the proven #49 pattern), E5 (new UI, layer discipline), C1–C3 (spec lives in issue bodies).

# Issue drafts — 2026-07-01 session (blocked from filing; run manually if approved)

## Draft 1 — THE diarization root cause

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] correctness: system tap ignores mid-session sample-rate changes — WAV timeline stretched ~1.6-1.9x, breaks diarization + transcript timestamps (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-tap-rate.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-tap-rate.md`)

**What's wrong.** `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` captures `inputFormat = newEngine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` once during `setupAggregateAndEngine` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144) and derives the AVAudioConverter ratio from it (`ratio = configuration.sampleRate / inputFormat.sampleRate`). There is **no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer on this engine** — unlike `MicCaptureActor`, which got exactly this handling in #49 (`MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`). When the tapped output device changes sample rate mid-session (e.g. Bluetooth headset renegotiating A2DP↔HFP when the mic engages — which THE RECORD itself triggers via `MicCaptureActor`), the tap keeps delivering buffers at the new rate while the converter still assumes the old one → time-stretched WAV.

**Evidence (production data, ~/Library/Application Support/THE RECORD).** Recording `F7C8DEAE-18DF-4853-B0D0-313FB81860BC` (2026-06-22): file birth→mtime 14:25:03→14:25:34 = **31 s wall time** (DB duration 31.195 s, mic-cleaned file 29.856 s — both agree), but main WAV `2026-06-22T20:25:03Z.wav` holds **57.685 s** @16 kHz (922,960 frames) = **1.85× wall time**. Signal analysis: zero duplicated blocks, no long-lag self-similarity (a 1 s probe matches only itself), pitch **bimodal** (~99 Hz and ~186 Hz clusters) → part of the session is rate-stretched, part normal → the rate changed mid-session. Second recording `F34D479A` (2026-06-18): WAV 10.085 s vs 6.23 s wall = **1.62×** — ratio varies with when the change occurred.

**Why it matters.** The main WAV is the single source of truth for the pipeline: batch transcription produces degraded text with timestamps on a fake 0–57.7 s timeline; diarization aligns speaker boundaries to that same corrupted audio (observed segments alternate "1"/"Unknown" across 0–57.68 s for a 31 s session). **This is the root cause of "diarization doesn't work."**

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the #49 fix on the system-tap engine: (1) observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild the converter+tap; (2) defensively compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` against the assumed rate inside the tap callback and rebuild on mismatch — the buffer's own format is authoritative; (3) log the change (relates to #194 — converter errors in this callback are currently silent).

Related: #49 (same bug fixed for MicCaptureActor), #194.

## Draft 2 — silent mic-cleaned WAV

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] correctness: mic-cleaned WAV is pure digital silence in production — AEC/sink chain writes no signal (AECProcessorActor.swift, WAVCleanedAudioSink)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-silent-mic.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-silent-mic.md`)

**What's wrong.** Both production `-mic-cleaned.wav` files (2026-06-18, 2026-06-22) contain **no signal at all**: average spectrum is −180 dB across every band 0–8 kHz. The file has the right duration (≈ wall time) but every sample is zero. So the mic → AEC → `CleanedAudioSink` chain runs, paces correctly, and writes silence.

**Why it matters.** The cleaned-mic track exists to feed the cleanup re-transcription pass (`cleaned_mic_audio_url`, `needs_retranscription`); a silent file means that pass transcribes nothing and the user's own voice is lost from the archive. Likely interacts with #190 (AEC truncates every mic buffer to 256 samples) and #192 (WAVWriter errorHandler never wired — failures invisible).

**Suggested fix.** Instrument the AEC output path with an RMS check (log if N consecutive cleaned buffers are all-zero); verify SpeexDSP echo-cancellation state isn't cancelling the entire near-end signal (e.g. mic signal fed as both near and far end); add an integration test asserting non-zero RMS through `AECProcessorActor` for a synthetic voice buffer.

Related: #190, #192, #231 (WAVCleanedAudioSink coupling).

## Draft 3 — stale word_timings on re-diarization

```bash
unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh issue create \
  --title "[see-something] silent-bug: attachDiarization upsert never clears word_timings — stale timings survive re-diarization (GRDBStorageActor+Diarization.swift:40)" \
  --label "see-something" \
  --body-file .temp/issue-body-word-timings.md
```

### Body (`.temp/issue-body-word-timings.md`)

**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.

**What's wrong.** `CoreAudioTapCaptureActor` captures `inputFormat = newEngine.inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)` once during `setupAggregateAndEngine` (CoreAudioTapCaptureActorSupport.swift:144) and derives the AVAudioConverter ratio from it (`ratio = configuration.sampleRate / inputFormat.sampleRate`). There is **no `AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange` observer on this engine** — unlike `MicCaptureActor`, which got exactly this handling in #49 (`MicCaptureActorRouteChange.swift`). When the tapped output device changes sample rate mid-session (e.g. Bluetooth headset renegotiating A2DP↔HFP when the mic engages — which THE RECORD itself triggers via `MicCaptureActor`), the tap keeps delivering buffers at the new rate while the converter still assumes the old one → time-stretched WAV.

**Evidence (production data, ~/Library/Application Support/THE RECORD).** Recording `F7C8DEAE-18DF-4853-B0D0-313FB81860BC` (2026-06-22): file birth→mtime 14:25:03→14:25:34 = **31 s wall time** (DB duration 31.195 s, mic-cleaned file 29.856 s — both agree), but main WAV `2026-06-22T20:25:03Z.wav` holds **57.685 s** @16 kHz (922,960 frames) = **1.85× wall time**. Signal analysis: zero duplicated blocks, no long-lag self-similarity (a 1 s probe matches only itself), pitch **bimodal** (~99 Hz and ~186 Hz clusters) → part of the session is rate-stretched, part normal → the rate changed mid-session. Second recording `F34D479A` (2026-06-18): WAV 10.085 s vs 6.23 s wall = **1.62×** — ratio varies with when the change occurred.

**Why it matters.** The main WAV is the single source of truth for the pipeline: batch transcription produces degraded text with timestamps on a fake 0–57.7 s timeline; diarization aligns speaker boundaries to that same corrupted audio (observed segments alternate "1"/"Unknown" across 0–57.68 s for a 31 s session). **This is the root cause of "diarization doesn't work."**

**Suggested fix.** Mirror the #49 fix on the system-tap engine: (1) observe `.AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange`, re-read `inputNode.inputFormat(forBus: 0)`, rebuild the converter+tap; (2) defensively compare `inBuffer.format.sampleRate` against the assumed rate inside the tap callback and rebuild on mismatch — the buffer's own format is authoritative; (3) log the change (relates to #194 — converter errors in this callback are currently silent).

Related: #49 (same bug fixed for MicCaptureActor), #194.

**What's wrong.** `attachDiarization` upserts segments via `GRDBSQL.upsertSegment`, whose `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` sets text/speaker/start/end/confidence but **not `word_timings`** — and `DiarizedSegment.wordTimings` from the incoming transcript is never written. `getSegments` reads `word_timings` back and attaches it to whatever text now occupies that `segment_index`.

**Why it matters.** After any re-diarization (repair pipeline, cleanup pass), segment N's text/boundaries change but its old `word_timings` JSON remains → word-level highlighting/alignment silently points at the wrong words.

**Suggested fix.** Either persist `seg.wordTimings` in the upsert (add the column to `upsertSegment` with excluded update), or explicitly `SET word_timings = NULL` on conflict so stale data can't survive.
